segments.line: That night, Nefer comes
running. Her
father went out with a team to bring copper tools back from the desert. A
sandstorm hit this afternoon. They
haven't come back.
Out there, at night, with no water, people don't last long. And the king's
soldiers won't search the desert in the dark for a few workers. You
look at the batteries. If you fly now, you use the full one. At
sunrise you'll have half a battery to show the king all of Egypt.
Djedi will make sure that isn't enough.
Nefer doesn't ask. She just looks
at you. You fly. You
keep the drone low and slow, under the wind, following the old track toward the copper mines. The
air still carries sand. The
screen goes brown, then clear, then brown again. The
desert at night is grey on black. Dunes. Rocks. Nothing.
Nefer is holding your sleeve so tight it hurts.
Forty percent. Thirty. Twenty. Then,
far out, a tiny orange dot. A fire. You
drop lower. Six people around it, waving at the sky. You
mark the spot, and the soldiers ride out. Then the screen
freezes. Signal lost. The
drone is behind a dune, kilometres away, in the dark. And then you
remember the rule.
Two minutes later you hear it. A buzz in the dark sky, getting louder.
Return to Home. It
lands in the sand, right at your feet.
Battery: nine percent. And
the sun is coming up.
